prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts the camera wearer moving from a kitchen/dining area into an adjacent dimly lit living room across the 5 frames: in Frame 1, a doorway wall and counter with a vase/flowers on the right are within arm's reach (~0.5–1.0 m) while a dining table on the left is ~2.5–3 m away and the living room beyond is >4 m deep; in Frames 2 and 3, the wearer approaches and passes beside the dining table (brightening to ~0.7–1.5 m directly in front and below, within arm's reach along with a water bottle on it and three surrounding chairs) while the partition wall behind the table stands at ~2.0–2.5 m and a pendant lamp hangs directly overhead (~1.0–1.5 m above). In Frames 4 and 5, as the wearer enters the living room and turns slightly right, the overhead ceiling lamp in Frame 4 passes very close (~0.5–0.8 m above), a foreground table surface with a tall narrow object/vase at the bottom center of Frame 5 enters arm's reach (~0.7–1.0 m), and the background couches on the left and wall/decorations on the right sit roughly 2.5–4.5 m away and 2–3 m apart from each other. The depth map clearly reveals the 3D geometry of the dim background living room furniture (sofas on the left, decorative stands on the right), the sharp depth discontinuity at the partition wall corner, and the tall foreground object in Frame 5 that is nearly invisible against the dark room in RGB. However, it is unreliable on the illuminated TV screen in the mid-ground (~3–4 m away), which is completely flattened into the background wall while the tall vertical object/figure standing just in front of the TV in Frame 4 (~2.5–3 m away) is only faintly resolved, and the deeply shadowed background corners in Frames 1–3 saturate to uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground objects across the progression: Frame 1 labels a `potted plant` on the right counter (~1 m away, within arm's reach) and mislabels a distant vertical shape or reflection near the living room on the left (~3.5 m away) as a `person`; Frame 2 captures the `dining table` (~1.2–2 m in front) flanked by three `chair` instances (left, behind, and right, spaced ~1 m apart) and a `bottle` on the tabletop (~1.5 m away), while Frame 3 retains only the top of the `bottle` at the bottom edge (~0.8 m, within arm's reach) as the table and chairs become largely cropped out of view below. In Frames 4 and 5, as the wearer steps into the living room, the map detects the `tv` on the right (~3–3.5 m away) and in Frame 4 labels both the vertical shape standing immediately in front of and partially occluding the `tv` (~2.8 m) and a small patch to the left near the sofa (~4 m) as `person`, whereas in Frame 5 only the `tv` mask remains with a cutout where it is occluded in front. While segmentation helps localize the small water bottle on the patterned tablecloth and highlights the occlusion cutout in front of the TV screen, it is highly unreliable in this low-light scene: it misses almost all background furniture (sofas, tables, lamps, walls) and hallucinated or ambiguously labeled `person` masks on dark vertical ornaments/vases, pillows, or figures displayed on the TV screen.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across Frames 1, 2, and 3, indicating no detected human bodies or hands near the dining area or within the camera wearer's own egocentric field of view. In Frames 4 and 5, a single small yellow body skeleton (with no magenta hand keypoints) appears in the lower-left to mid-left region corresponding to the dimly lit sofa area roughly 3.5–4.5 m in front of and to the left of the camera wearer, well beyond arm's reach. Based on the compact, horizontal arrangement of the torso and limb keypoints, this detected figure is reclined or seated on the couch, oriented roughly sideways/rightward in Frame 4 and shifting or rotating slightly as the camera turns right in Frame 5, with head keypoints indistinct and not clearly facing the camera wearer, while the lower body is occluded by the sofa cushions and dark shadows. Although the pose detector potentially picks up a person resting on the dark couch in Frames 4–5 that is almost impossible to discern in the underexposed RGB frames, it is unreliable because the keypoints are cramped and noisy—possibly misfiring on the patterned sofa pillows—and it completely misses any person in Frames 1–3 as well as the vertical shape segmentation labeled as a `person` in front of the TV.
